findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair:

1. The triple sink’s caulking is in disrepair and needs re-sealed. 
2. SECOND REPEAT- The front handwashing sink is observed to not be sealed to the wall. Ensure that this is sealed. 
3. There is trim missing on the wall to the right of the ice machine. The missing trim is exposing bare wood. Ensure that this trim is replaced. 

These repairs were discussed with the PIC. Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The floor in the back area and in the mop closet is observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on it. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The triple sink sanitizer solution in the kitchen was observed measuring at 100 ppm quaternary ammonium. CORRECTED- The person in charge was notified and the sanitizer dispenser was observed to be dispensing the appropriate amount of sanitizer (200 ppm). Test sanitizer solution and bucket regularly to ensure sanitizer solutions are effective at sanitizing food-contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(E) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (E) If a chemical SANITIZER other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Multiple surfaces were observed to be soiled:
1) Soda nozzles at self service station. CORRECTED- person in charge wiped soda dispenser surfaces and replaced nozzles with a second set so that the first set may be cleaned and sanitized.
2) The plastic wall-mounted knife holder was soiled. CORRECTED- person in charge cleaned the knife holder.
3) The ice machine was observed to have a build up of water residue around the power inlet. CORRECTED- person in charge emptied and cleaned the ice machine.

Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of soil, food, or water residue.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following physical facilities are in need of repair:
1) REPEAT: There were gaps observed between the front hand sink and the wall. Clean off existing caulking and re-seal the front hand sink to the wall.
2) REPEAT: There is a horizontal gash in the wall above the front hand sink. Fill in or patch the damaged wall.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Grease accumulation was observed on the fronts of the fryers.  Clean the fryers.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The following physical facilities are in need of repair:
1) There are gaps and crevices present between the front handsink and the wall, some of which are within or created by the existing caulking. Clean off existing caulking and re-seal the front handsink to the wall.
2) There is a horizontal gash in the wall above the front handsink. Fill or patch the damaged wall.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: REPEAT: Floor tile was damaged and had accumulation of mold/general buildup on the right side of the 3 part sink floor drain. Clean and repair the floor in this area.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Mold was starting to accumulate on surfaces around the ice maker in the ice machine. Ensure ice machine is cleaned and sanitized as needed to eliminate buildup of mold.
Equipment such as ice bins, beverage dispensing nozzles, and enclosed components such as ice makers shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-202.16 Soiled cardboard was observed lining shelves in the walk-in cooler. Replace the cardboard. If using cardboard to line shelves, it needs to be replaced at a frequency that does not allow for buildup of soil and/or apparent evidence of being worn from use. Otherwise, provide a durable, easily cleanable liner, such as baking sheets or hard plastic.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 Floor tile was damaged and had accumulation of mold/general buildup on the right side of the 3 part sink floor drain. Clean and repair the floor in this area.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Three part sink floor drain was heavily soiled with buildup of mold/general debris. Clean the floor drain as needed and maintain it clean.
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee arrived to work and did not wash hands prior to getting ice to fill the soda machine. Handwashing was discussed, and employee washed his hands before continuing with next task. Ensure handwashing occurs upon arrival to work and prior to handling food and/or working with equipment and single service articles.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat solution in front service area sani-bucket was observed at 100ppm. Employee noted the solution dispensed at a concentration of 400-500ppm, so water was added to bring down concentration. A fresh solution was dispensed and observed at 200ppm. Owner noted fluctuation in concentration occurs depending on temperature of water used to make solutions. Ensure solutions are prepared with water at an appropriate temperature to provide a concentration of 200-400ppm as required by product label directions. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Mold was starting to accumulate on surfaces around the ice maker in the ice machine. Cleaning frequency was discussed.
Equipment such as ice bins, beverage dispensing nozzles, and enclosed components such as ice makers shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-202.16 Bottom shelf of prep table by ice machine was worn and rusty. Clean and resurface the bottom shelf of the prep table to provide a surface that is smooth and easy to clean.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 PIC is working to complete certification. Online course was attempted but needed to be changed to an in-person course due to compatibility issues. PIC plans to have food manager certification completed by next routine inspection.
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority item for sanitization was observed. Staff were unaware the sanitizer dispenser was not functioning properly. Manager left in charge after the owner left for the day does not currently have a food manager certification. Active managerial controls were discussed and will be revisited at the followup inspection on 3/31/22. 
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 The owner is currently the only employee with a food manager certification. The manager who has an expired certification is registered to complete food manager course this weekend.
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) A food employee rehired at the facility within the last few weeks did not have a signed reporting agreement on file. Owner had the employee review and sign a reporting agreement during the inspection. Additional copies of the reporting agreement were provided, and employee health policy was discussed. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring and sign reporting agreements prior to beginning their first shift. Maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff. Make sure reporting agreements are signed again and provided if/when employees cease employment but are later rehired. 
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Paper towel dispenser at handwashing sink by 3 part sink was not working properly. A red light indicated the batteries were in need of changing. Extra batteries were not available for replacement. Paper towels were removed and placed on top of the dispenser to allow for access and promote proper handwashing.
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with Individual, disposable towels or another approved drying option.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Freshly dispensed quat solution in a sani-bucket registered at 100-150ppm with inspector’s instant change test strips and facility’s litmus paper strips. Additional product was manually mixed in the solution to provide a concentration of 400ppm. Bi-weekly service for the dispenser is scheduled to occur the morning of 3/31/22. Inspector will return the afternoon of 3/31/22 to check the dispenser. In the meantime, sanitizer solutions will be mixed manually by adding additional product to dispensed solutions to allow for proper concentration of 200-400ppm as required for product being used. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 1. Mold was observed on the backside of the ice shoot and at the soda machine where nozzles attach. 
2. Mold was starting to accumulate on surfaces around the ice maker in the ice machine.
Cleaning frequency for the aforementioned equipment was discussed. 
Equipment such as ice bins, beverage dispensing nozzles, and enclosed components such as ice makers shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11 Spray bottle containing a light yellow liquid was observed in the same area as sani-bucket storage. Bottle contained degreaser and was labeled as to the contents. 
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Allergen certifications expired in January and February of 2022. Manager registered to take a food manager course this weekend is also scheduled to renew the allergen certification. Owner stated they will work on renewing allergen certification this weekend as well. 
Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Mold was observed on the backside of the ice shoot and in a few of the nozzles at the fountain soda machine. Cleaning frequency was discussed. 
Equipment such as beverage dispensing nozzles and enclosed components shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Sliced gyro meat hot holding on the grill was observed with internal temperatures at 117F-128F. PIC reheated product to 165F. Ensure proper hot holding at 135F/above after meat has been heated to proper cook temperature.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Quat test kit was water damaged. New test kit will be purchased tomorrow. 
A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions in mg/L shall be provided.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: 4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria. Quat sanitizer in the 3 part sink is observed between 100 - 150 ppm concentration. Facility is in the process of switching between a pre-mixed machine solution to tablets. Inspector discussed setting up an in house system to understand how many tablets would be needed for a set amount of water. Inspector discussed with the PIC as well as the current dish washer. The sink was remade during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment: 3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less.  Surface temperatures of foods in the top of the prep cooler were above 50F. Internal temperature of foods in the top holding area ranged from 50F-51F internal temperatures.  Foods in the bottom reach-in section were observed with internal temperatures of 45F-46F (diced tomatoes). PIC stated that all TCS foods were opened, removed from the freezer, or prepared fresh this morning around 11am. All TCS foods in the prep cooler were to be used or discarded by 5pm based on information provided. Air masters was contacted during the inspection to conduct maintenance on the machine. Inspector will spot check to ensure compliance.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. 

The caulking around the hand sink adjacent to the kitchen area is observed with significant degradation. A seam was also observed above the sink in the wall as well as a gap around where a pipe inserts into the wall to the left of the paper towels. PIC is instructed to repair the surfaces so that they are smooth and easily cleanable.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 PIC began drying hands with dispensed paper towels and then shut off the manual faucet prior to fully drying hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.
Hands should be thoroughly dried prior to using the paper towels to shut off the faucet. Once paper towels are used to shut off the faucet they are contaminated. If additional drying of hands is needed, use soiled paper towels to touch the handle of the dispenser to retrieve new paper towels to finish drying hands instead of continuing to use the paper towels just used to shut off the faucet.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Surface temperatures of foods in the top of the prep cooler were above 50F. Internal temperature of foods in the top holding area ranged from 49F-50F (American cheese slices; front right corner) to 56F (green relish; left side). Foods in the bottom reach-in section were observed with internal temperatures of 55F (gyro chicken; left side), 52F (dressing; middle), and 47F-48F (green relish; right side). A portion of dressing prepared the day prior were discarded. All other foods were opened, removed from the freezer, or prepared fresh this morning around 11am. All TCS foods in the prep cooler were to be used or discarded by 5pm based on information provided.  
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Prep cooler was not functioning properly and unable to maintain TCS foods at 41F/below. Thermometer inside the bottom reach-in section was reading between 30F-40F but was broken (see #36 for details). Inspector placed stem thermometers in the bottom reach-in section on the left side and right side. Thermometer on the left side was reading between 50F-60F, while thermometer on the right side was reading closer to 50F. Cooler was failing, and a call for service was made. Technician arrived during inspection for service. Freon was added, and the temperature dropped to 40F during service. (see general comments for additional information.
Equipment holding cold food shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain proper temperature of TCS foods.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204-112 Thermometers in cold holding units were not reading accurately. The thermometer in the bottom of the prep cooler was reading between 30F-40F and when moved to the chest freezer did not move at all. The thermometer in the chest freezer was reading below -20F and was placed in the bottom of the prep cooler to check the temperature. That thermometer also read between 30F and 40F despite the cooler holding above 50F. Also, a thermometer in the freezer section of the fridge/freezer unit was not working. New thermometers will be purchased for placement in all cold holding units.
Cold or hot holding equipment used for time/temperature  control for safety (TCS) food shall be designed to include and shall be equipped with at least one permanently affixed temperature measuring device that is located to allow easy viewing of the device's temperature display.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 Handsink in back by the 3 part sink was soiled with grimy buildup. Clean the back handsink as needed and maintain it clean.
--Mopsink was observed with general buildup and mold. Clean the mopsink daily/as needed to eliminate buildup.
--Lower right section of drywall between mopsink and storage shelving was damaged. Re-seal the area where damage has occurred.
--Floor drain under 3 part sink was soiled with heavy buildup down inside as well as on the underside of the grated cover located on top of the drain. Clean the floor drain and cover as needed to eliminate buildup. 
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Plastic tub with French fries in the chest freezer was observed without a lid. Also, frozen pastry bag was observed open in the walkin freezer. Make sure containers and packages of food are covered and closed for long-term, overnight storage.
Food shall be protected from cross contamination by storing food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114 Quat solution in a spray bottle at the front counter had a concentration of 0ppm. Owner noted the spray bottle of sanitizer does not get used; staff use the sani-bucket during hours of operation. Solution was emptied and spray bottle was discarded. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.12 Dried food splash and food debris were observed inside the microwave. Cleaning frequency was discussed. 
The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 Feta cheese in the prep cooler had a date mark of 9/9, which was last Monday. Owner was advised that 9/9 starts the 7 day time frame and the product was discarded. Ensure that foods prepared on Monday and require date marking are used or discarded by the end of the business day on Saturday since facility is closed on Sunday.

Open hummus, washed/cut lettuce, thawed/pre-cooked chicken breasts, and sliced/diced tomatoes in cold holding were all without date marks. Based on information provided, all products were prepared for use as of the Saturday prior. Proper dates were provided.
Refrigerated, ready to eat, time/temperature control for safety food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature 41F/less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12 Plastic spoon was observed in open hummus with the handle down in the product. Spoon was removed and discarded.
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14 A chlorine test kit was available for use, but quat sanitizer is used at the facility. Owner noted they just ran out of strips over the weekend and he must have purchased the wrong strips. Inspector had some extra quat strips for facility to use until a new test kit can be purchased later today. 
A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions shall be provided. Obtain and use quat test strips with sanitizer used on food contact surfaces in the kitchen.
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 Sanitizer solution was not yet prepared and available for use during morning prep. Solution was made available.
Sanitizing solution shall be provided and available for use during all hours of prep and operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 The following nonfood contact surfaces were observed to be soiled:
A) catch pan under soda machine (old soda splash);
B) counter under soda machine (dust/splash); and
C) outer surfaces of counter-top fryer (grease).
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.citation_text:
5-402.13 Sani-bucket containing old solution from Saturday was observed. Proper disposal of waste water was discussed. Solution was discarded and fresh sanitizer prepared for current day of operation. 
All sewage and waste water must be routed to an approved sewage disposal system. Properly dispose of sani-bucket solutions after use and do not leave it sitting in the facility overnight.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text:
6-303.11 Light in the walkin cooler used for dry storage did not turn on. Owner noted it doesn't work right and sometimes comes on intermittently. Repair the light so it works properly.
The light intensity shall be at least 10 foot candles (108 lux) at a 30 inches above the floor, in walk-in refrigeration units and dry food storage areas and in other areas and rooms during periods of cleaning.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Food employee was observed touching the handle of the paper towel dispenser upon completing handwashing process. Employee was advised to use paper towels as a barrier to touch the handles of the manual faucet and handle of the paper towel dispenser once hands are washed to avoid re-contamination of freshly washed hands. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink and paper towel dispensers. Use of forearms and elbows to dispense paper towels would also be acceptable.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Mold buildup was observed in the ice machine around the ice tray. Clean and sanitize inside the ice machine. 
Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-203.11 Metal stem thermometer was reading at 20°F when checked in ice water. Thermometer was properly calibrated to 32°F in the ice water solution. Cleaning and maintenance of food thermometers were discussed.
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Hood was observed to have buildup of grease. PIC noted the hood was due for cleaning and would be done in the near future.
Wall and pipes behind cook line were soiled with grease. Clean behind the equipment daily/as needed. 
Back handsink was soiled with buildup in the basin. Clean the handsinks and related fixtures daily/as needed.
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.
